items.rationale: The rug was soaked only by the robot's preventable spread, so §§3.3(j) and 7.1.11 exclude its handling. If covered, ordinary removal and transport would be about €85.
The dedicated light shares the table's €500 gross limit under §§4.8.2–4.8.3, which is allocated entirely to the cloth. If payable separately, §7.1.9 would limit it to equivalent pre-loss lighting.

Cleaning would ordinarily be the first remedy under §7.1.10, but §§3.3(j) and 7.1.11 exclude the rug because it was wet only in the preventably enlarged area. Comparable cleaning would be about €230 if covered.
Section 7.1.7(i) covers inspection to establish damage and repairability even if the item itself is not indemnified. Allow about €95 for a basic diagnostic inspection.
Sections 3.3(i) and 7.1.11 exclude damage the vacuum sustained to itself while operating after water contact. A comparable replacement would be about €350 if covered.
Disassembly falls within the table's shared €500 cap under §4.8.3. The aggregate exceeds the cap, so the cloth line takes the full allowance; standalone disassembly would be about €155.
The specific rule in §4.8.3 includes inspection in the table cap and gives the entire allowance to the cloth when aggregate costs exceed €500. Standalone inspection would be about €110.
The table, accessories and related work exceed the per-item limit. Section 4.8.3 assigns the full €500 including VAT to renewal of the playing-surface covering, not a pro rata share.
The cues are accessories under §4.8.2, and §4.8.3 allocates the full €500 to the cloth. Comparable cues would be about €110 if separately payable.
Alignment and reassembly are included in the shared cap under §4.8.3, which is exhausted by the cloth line. The standalone work would be about €250.

The hobby-room ceiling was damaged by direct water migration and qualifies for like-for-like repair under §§7.1.1(b) and 7.1.5. Allow 8 m² at about €80/m², excluding separately billed opening and finishing.

Sections 7.1.5–7.1.7 cover filling on the damaged ceiling or documented affected wall areas, but not undamaged walls or work already included in ceiling reinstatement. Allow about €255 for the separately attributable finishing work.
Sections 5.2.1 and 7.1.8(a), (c) allow one site-wide removal of repair debris and residues, not general cleaning. If this charge is for that covered cleanup, the reference threshold is €208.
Section 7.1.7(b), (e) covers necessary drying equipment for directly affected areas. The comparable three-fan lines support about €81 total.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers drying-progress checks, and §7.1.8(c) distinguishes them from initial and final measurements. Allow two checks at about €105 each.
Section 7.1.7(b) covers a distinct completion check before reinstatement. Allow about €125 for the final reading and record.
The WC floor was in the direct escape-of-water path, and §7.1.7(a) covers necessary removal. Allow 5 m² at about €45/m² for an unspecified floor finish.
Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.7(a), (d) cover removal related to directly affected flooring, but not trim removed solely for the robot-spread patch. Allow about €85 for the covered portion of the 12 m run.
Section 7.1.7(b) expressly covers concealed layers where water migrated through the floor build-up. Allow €480 for the layer-drying work, excluding separately charged equipment.
Section 7.1.7(b), (e) covers necessary dryer hire for the directly affected areas. The two-unit reference threshold is €123 gross.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers compressor hire needed for concealed-layer drying if it is not already included in the drying charge under §7.1.8(c). Allow €155 for one hire charge.

items.description: Remove parquet in direct drip zone
items.rationale: The 6 m² drip zone was damaged by direct water migration, independently of the vacuum. Section 7.1.7(a) covers removal at about €35/m², or €210.

items.description: Renew parquet in direct drip zone
items.rationale: Sections 7.1.5 and 7.1.9 permit like-for-like reinstatement of the 6 m² direct drip zone. Allow about €120/m² including installation, or €720.

items.description: Renew additional parquet wetted by robot
items.rationale: Sections 3.3(j) and 7.1.11 exclude the additional area because the homeowner saw the vacuum spreading water and could have stopped it. If covered, a small patch of ordinary parquet removal and renewal would be about €850.
Section 7.1.7(d) does not cover trim that broke during repair of the excluded robot-spread patch. Allow about €350 for the directly affected portion of the 12 m line at roughly €40/m.
Opening the documented wet ceiling is necessary dismantling under §7.1.7(a), distinct from restoring it under §7.1.8(c). Allow 8 m² at about €32/m², rounded to €255.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers tracing the escape to the cistern fill valve. Allow €195 for a straightforward investigation, excluding separately billed travel, moisture mapping and dismantling.
Sections 7.1.7(b), (i) cover initial mapping of water migration across rooms, distinct from progress and completion checks under §7.1.8(c). Allow €245, in line with comparable multi-area surveys.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers dismantling needed to reach the defective valve. Allow €105 for this operation to the extent it is distinct from the cause investigation and separately billed labour.
Section 7.1.7(e) covers renewal of the part from which water escaped at standard-grade cost. Allow €85 for the valve and fitting work not billed elsewhere.
Sections 7.1.7(g) and 7.1.8(c) allow customary labour only if the hours are not already included in the cistern charges. If separately supported, the three-hour reference threshold is €226.
Section 7.1.7(f) allows the first travel, mileage or call-out charge on the plumber's invoice. The vehicle charge is the only one separately identified, and the reference threshold is €84.
